== Example Question ==
What is the answer to this question?

[[File:Find the mistake.png|frameless]]

== 90% ==
How many hands are in this picture?

[[File:Hands.png|frameless]]

'''6''': Two holding the phone and another four in the photograph.

== 80% ==
When spelt out in words, which one of these comes first alphabetically?

[[File:1% Club 2.png|frameless]]

The C for ‘Club’ comes before the O for ‘One’ and the P for ‘Percent’.

==70%==
{| class="fandom-table"
! colspan="2" |What WORD has more letters in it?
|-
|'''envelope'''
|postbox
|}
It’s just a counting question. Envelope has eight letters and postbox has seven.

==60%==
{| class="fandom-table"
! colspan="3" |Answer the following question: Pwhich pof thep follopwing plives pin thep seap?
|-
|BOLT
|'''CLAMP'''
|SCREW
|}
Every word has an additional ‘P’ so the question should read ‘Which of the following lives in the sea?’ and the answer is CLAM.

== 50% ==
'''Which''' is the longest word in this question that contains none of the letters of the word ‘One’?

== 45% ==
If “left” is “right” and “wrong” is also “right”, what is “easy” and also “soft”?

'''Hard''': They are all opposites.

== 40% ==
Which word in the question below sounds like the odd one out?

Why are you '''out'''?

All the others sound like letters: Why is Y, are is R, you is U, but out is just out.

== 35% ==
[[File:OandX.png|frameless]]
{| class="fandom-table"
! colspan="2" |Crosses have won, but who went first in this game of Noughts and Crosses?
|-
|Noughts
|Crosses
|}
Although both ‘Noughts’ and ‘Crosses’ have played four moves each, ‘Crosses’ was the last to play, because it won the game by getting three in a row. That means that ‘Noughts’ must have gone first.

== 30% ==
A brother and sister take their dog for a walk. The sister jogs at an average of 8mph while the boy walks at an average of 4mph. The dog runs at a constant 10mph back and forth between them and he does not stop at any point. After an hour how far will the dog have run?

'''10 miles''': The dog runs at 10mph. The miles and speed of the brother and sister are irrelevant.

== 25% ==
{| class="fandom-table"
! colspan="4" |Which one of these UK towns is the odd one out?
|-
|Sidmouth
|Gateshead
|Hitchin
|'''Whitby'''
|}
It is the only one that does not end with a body part.

== 20% ==
Which four-letter word is missing from this list?

spot<br>opts<br>pots<br>stop<br>tops<br>'''post'''

It is the only other word that can be made from those four letters.

==15% ==
If 2, 3 and 10 go together, and 6 and 7 go together, which two out of 1, 4, 5, 8 and 9 are a pair?

'''4 and 5''': Numbers are grouped with numbers with which they share a first letter.

== 10% ==
What is the total of the four pieces of arithmetic seen here?

[[File:Maths.png|frameless]]

(8+3 = 11), (4×2 = 8), (7+5 = 12), (1×2 = 2)

11 + 8 + 12 + 2 = 33

== 5% ==
What unusual pattern do these words have in common?

FIRST<br>ALMOST<br>BEGIN<br>EMPTY<br>BELOW

They are all words that have their letters in alphabetical order.

==1%==
What four-letter word fits into the gaps in the sentences below so that they all make sense?

'''Only''' I am certain that he had read the man’s notes.

I am certain that '''only''' he had read the man’s notes.

I am certain that he had read the man’s '''only''' notes.
